learner_notice: Commit one response before feedback appears. Entry checks are low stakes, and unresolved prerequisite mapping returns to V3-LES-386478.

items.title: Starting check: locate the conclusion
items.prompt: Passage: “The community archive extended weekend hours last spring. Weekend visits then increased. The archive director therefore argues that the added hours improved access for people unavailable on weekdays.” Which statement is the conclusion?
options: The archive changed its schedule last spring
The added hours improved access beyond weekdays
Weekend visits increased after the schedule changed
The archive records visits during each weekend
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Guided practice: test a direct inference
items.prompt: Passage: “Every proposal accepted in this round included a cost estimate. Proposal K was accepted in this round. Therefore Proposal K included a cost estimate.” How should the reasoning be evaluated using only the passage?
options: Unsupported because acceptance never relates to estimates
Merely plausible because the passage discusses one proposal
Supported by the passage’s universal premise
Unsound because outside facts about Proposal K are missing
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Less help: preserve a qualifier
items.prompt: Passage: “In several surveyed workshops, shorter meetings were associated with higher attendance. The author concludes that shortening any meeting will always increase attendance.” What is the central logic problem?
options: It turns a limited association into an absolute rule
The conclusion is too cautious about the surveyed workshops
The passage proves that meeting length never matters
The author supplies too many definitions of attendance
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: On your own: find a missing bridge
items.prompt: Passage: “Reviewers praised the plan’s clear organization. The author concludes that the plan will receive the largest grant.” Which evaluation best fits?
options: The conclusion follows because clarity guarantees the largest award
The conclusion contradicts the statement that reviewers praised clarity
The conclusion is outside the passage because grants do not exist
The conclusion needs an unstated bridge from clarity to award size
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Near exit: judge conclusion fit
items.prompt: Passage: “The town’s two pilot kiosks reduced average permit wait time. Both kiosks used the same simplified form. The council concludes that adopting the simplified form at offices with the same paperwork bottleneck is likely to reduce waits.” Which evaluation is strongest?
options: Unreasonable because a conclusion may never use “likely”
Reasonable because it keeps the condition and uncertainty
Certain because two pilots prove every office will improve
Irrelevant because wait time cannot support a claim about wait time
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Changed exit: select a warranted revision
items.prompt: Passage: “A critic argues that public murals always unify neighborhoods. The critic later notes that one mural prompted prolonged disagreement about whose history it represented.” Which revised conclusion best fits the passage?
options: Public murals never influence neighborhood identity
Disagreement proves that the mural had no public meaning
Murals can prompt discussion without always creating unity
Every neighborhood must remove murals that prompt disagreement
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Repair: compare support and conclusion
items.prompt: Which question most directly tests whether a conclusion fits its passage support?
options: Does the conclusion exceed the support’s scope or certainty?
Do I personally agree with the conclusion’s topic?
Can I recall an outside example that uses similar words?
Is the conclusion the longest sentence in the passage?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Fresh re-entry: evaluate a new qualified claim
items.prompt: Passage: “Three branches that added a text reminder saw fewer missed appointments. The author concludes that branches serving similar clients may reduce missed appointments by adding the same reminder.” Which evaluation fits?
options: Unsupported because the conclusion mentions branches
Reasonable because it keeps similarity and possibility
Certain because three observations establish a universal law
Contradictory because reminders and appointments are unrelated in the passage
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Repair: use a counterexample correctly
items.prompt: An argument claims that an action “always” has one result, and the passage supplies one clear case where it does not. What follows?
options: The action must always have the opposite result
The entire passage becomes meaningless
The absolute “always” claim is not sustained as written
The counterexample proves every qualified version false
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Fresh re-entry: revise another absolute claim
items.prompt: Passage: “The essay claims that digital maps always reduce exploration. It also describes hikers who used a digital map to locate an unfamiliar trail and then explored beyond it.” Which conclusion best fits?
options: Digital maps can never affect exploration
The hikers did not use a digital map
All hikers explore more when using digital maps
Digital maps do not invariably reduce exploration
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Starting check: identify relevant evidence
items.prompt: Claim: “The speaker values firsthand observation.” Which passage detail is most relevant?
options: The speech was delivered in a large hall
The speaker’s notebook has a blue cover
The speaker contrasts observations with rumors
The audience entered through two doors
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Guided practice: separate relevance from sufficiency
items.prompt: Passage: “One reader praised the novel’s ending.” Claim: “All readers found the ending satisfying.” How should the quoted evidence be evaluated?
options: Relevant but insufficient for a claim about all readers
Irrelevant because praise can never indicate satisfaction
Sufficient because one reader represents every reader
Absent because the passage contains no reader response
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Less help: find an irrelevant detail
items.prompt: Claim: “The committee opposed the proposed closing date.” Which detail is least relevant?
options: Members called the deadline unworkable
The final vote rejected the date
Several members requested a later date
The meeting room had twelve windows
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: On your own: evaluate silence
items.prompt: A short passage describes three paintings selected for an exhibit but never claims to list the full exhibit. The passage does not mention sculpture. What can be concluded from that silence?
options: The exhibit certainly prohibited sculpture
Silence alone does not show sculpture was absent
Sculpture was the exhibit’s main focus
The three paintings were not actually selected
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Near exit: judge an evidence set
items.prompt: Claim: “The revised signs made the route easier to follow.” Passage evidence: visitors made fewer wrong turns after the revision and several explicitly credited the new arrows. Which evaluation best fits?
options: Irrelevant because signs cannot be discussed in route evidence
Absent because no visitor is named
Relevant and sufficient for this bounded claim
Sufficient to prove every route everywhere is easy
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Changed exit: choose evidence that closes a gap
items.prompt: Passage claim: “The editor rejected the essay because its evidence was incomplete.” The passage currently reports only that the essay was rejected. Which added detail would most directly support the stated reason?
options: The editor says the central claim lacks support
The essay was submitted on a Tuesday morning
The editor has worked at the journal for six years
The journal’s cover uses a geometric design
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Repair: run the two-link evidence test
items.prompt: Which pair of questions best evaluates a passage detail offered for a claim?
options: Is the detail memorable, and is it written first?
Is the detail outside the passage, and do I agree with it?
Is the sentence long, and does it use a vivid image?
Does it bear on the claim, and is it enough?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Fresh re-entry: evaluate converging details
items.prompt: Claim: “The new index helped readers locate topics.” Passage evidence: search time fell after the index was added, and readers described using its cross-references. Which evaluation fits?
options: Irrelevant because an index is not a topic
Relevant and sufficient for these readers
Absent because the index entries are not reproduced
Sufficient to prove every index helps every reader
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Repair: identify the missing warrant
items.prompt: A passage reports an outcome and then assigns a specific reason for it. What evidence is most needed?
options: A decorative detail from the same paragraph
A fact that the outcome occurred at some time
A passage link from the proposed reason to the outcome
An outside fact unrelated to the author’s account
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Fresh re-entry: choose a direct supporting detail
items.prompt: Claim: “The curator moved the sculpture to improve visibility.” Which added passage sentence most directly supports the stated purpose?
options: The curator says the old corner hid the work
The sculpture was made several decades earlier
The gallery floor was polished on the same day
Visitors entered through a wooden door
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Starting check: preserve the observed group
items.prompt: Passage: “Four coastal libraries surveyed this summer reported more evening visitors after extending hours.” Which conclusion stays within the stated basis?
options: The surveyed libraries reported more evening visitors
Every library gains visitors whenever it extends hours
All coastal institutions should remain open at night
Libraries in every season respond identically
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Guided practice: detect population drift
items.prompt: Passage: “Two first-year seminars used weekly peer review, and their enrolled students submitted more revisions.” Which claim goes beyond the basis?
options: Students in the two seminars submitted more revisions
The pattern occurred in the observed first-year seminars
Weekly peer review accompanied more revisions in those groups
Weekly peer review makes every university student revise more
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Less help: track a condition
items.prompt: Passage: “When the trail was dry, the lighter boots reduced travel time for the tested hikers.” Which conclusion best preserves the condition?
options: Lighter boots always reduce travel time under every weather condition
Tested hikers were faster in lighter boots on the dry trail
Every hiker on every trail should avoid all heavier boots
Wet trails necessarily produce the same travel-time difference
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: On your own: compare time scope
items.prompt: Passage: “During one festival week, buses on Route 7 carried more passengers after service was added.” Which claim is least warranted?
options: Route 7 carried more passengers during the observed festival week
The added service coincided with more Route 7 passengers that week
Route 7 will carry more passengers every week of every year
The observation concerns a festival-week service change
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Near exit: evaluate a generalization
items.prompt: Passage: “Three small museums in one city added free Friday entry, and Friday attendance rose at each.” The author concludes: “Free Friday entry may raise Friday attendance at similar small museums in that city.” Which evaluation fits?
options: Unwarranted because no conclusion may extend beyond identical buildings
Certain because three cases establish a universal rule
Irrelevant because museums cannot be compared
Reasonable because it preserves the stated limits
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Changed exit: revise an overgeneralization
items.prompt: Passage: “Five residents of one apartment building preferred the new courtyard seating.” Which revision is best supported?
options: The interviewed residents preferred the new seating
All city residents prefer courtyard seating
Every apartment building should copy the design
No resident could dislike the new seating
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Repair: build the scope box
items.prompt: Which inventory most directly checks a passage generalization?
options: Population, setting, time, conditions, and quantifier
Sentence length, punctuation, font, and paragraph count
Outside examples, personal experience, and topic familiarity
Author biography, publication date, and cover design
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Fresh re-entry: evaluate a bounded extension
items.prompt: Passage: “Two neighborhood clinics using the same reminder system reported fewer missed morning visits.” Claim: “Similar clinics using that system may see fewer missed morning visits.” How should it be evaluated?
options: Unsupported because “clinics” appears in both evidence and claim
Reasonable for explicitly similar clinics
Certain for every clinic and every appointment type
Contradicted because the passage mentions mornings
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Repair: correct a quantifier shift
items.prompt: Evidence concerns “some members of the selected group.” Which conclusion keeps the same quantifier strength?
options: No member of the group has the feature
Every member of every group has the feature
Some members of the selected group have the feature
Most people everywhere must have the feature
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Fresh re-entry: revise a seasonal claim
items.prompt: Passage: “Six farms in the valley reported lower water use during a cool spring after installing timers.” Which conclusion is best supported?
options: Timers always lower water use in every climate
All farms should expect the same annual result
Cool springs eliminate the need for irrigation
The six farms used less water that cool spring
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Starting check: identify causal language
items.prompt: Which sentence makes a causal claim rather than reporting sequence or association?
options: Attendance rose after the schedule changed
Attendance and later hours appeared together
Later hours were associated with attendance
The schedule change produced the rise in attendance
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Guided practice: test sequence alone
items.prompt: Passage: “Complaints declined after a new form appeared.” The author concludes that the form caused the decline. No other link is supplied. Which evaluation fits?
options: The claim is certain because the form appeared first
Relevant sequence, but insufficient for causation
The claim is impossible because forms never affect complaints
The passage proves complaints caused the form
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Less help: use a passage-supplied alternative
items.prompt: Passage: “Waits shortened after online booking began, but the office also doubled staffing that morning.” Which conclusion is best supported?
options: Online booking alone certainly caused the shorter waits
Staffing cannot affect waits because booking is mentioned first
The passage does not isolate booking from added staffing
Shorter waits caused both booking and staffing
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: On your own: recognize direct linkage
items.prompt: Passage: “A lamp flickers whenever connector C is loosened, stops flickering when C is tightened, and flickers again when C is loosened.” Which claim is best warranted?
options: Loosening connector C causes this lamp to flicker
Every lamp flicker everywhere is caused by connector C
The flicker causes connector C to loosen
Connector C has no relation to the flicker
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Near exit: evaluate a causal conclusion
items.prompt: Passage: “Errors fell after a checklist was introduced. The same week, workers received extra training, which the passage says addressed the most common error.” The author claims the checklist alone caused the decline. Which evaluation is strongest?
options: Supported because the checklist is named before training
Supported because every later event is caused by the first event
Contradicted because checklists can never help
Not warranted because training is a passage-supported alternative
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Changed exit: interpret intervention reversal
items.prompt: Passage sequence: a display is clear; a tinted cover is added and the display becomes dim; the cover is removed and clarity returns; the same cover is replaced and dimness returns. Which conclusion best fits?
options: The display became dim only because time passed
The cover causes the described dimness
Dimness caused the cover to be installed
Every tinted object dims every display
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Repair: separate timing from linkage
items.prompt: What must a passage add to “B happened after A” before a causal conclusion is warranted?
options: A longer description of B’s appearance
A statement that A was mentioned first
A passage link from changed A to changed B
An unrelated outside example
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Fresh re-entry: test another simultaneous change
items.prompt: Passage: “Sales rose after the store changed its window display, but prices were also reduced that day and the passage notes many buyers mentioned the discounts.” Can the display-alone causal claim be sustained?
options: No; the price reduction is a supported alternative
Yes; the display is mentioned before prices
Yes; any event before an outcome is its only cause
No; sales can never respond to displays
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Repair: recognize an intervention pattern
items.prompt: Which passage pattern most directly strengthens a bounded causal link?
options: The outcome is described with vivid language
The factor and outcome are mentioned in one paragraph
The outcome occurs once long after the factor
The outcome tracks the factor’s removal and return
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Fresh re-entry: evaluate a restored condition
items.prompt: Passage: “A tone sounds when switch S is pressed, stops when S is released, and sounds again when S is pressed while all described settings stay fixed.” Which conclusion is warranted?
options: The tone causes the switch to move
Pressing S causes the tone in this setup
Every switch produces the same tone
Time alone causes alternating sound and silence
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.
